decisions.evidence: R3 maker: metadata shown as 'title, site, and a description appear on their own', favicon rendered as 'just a letter', no preview image. R3 client: 'I'd also expect the page's real icon and preview image when available, rather than just a letter.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-02 requires favicon+preview image auto-collected; presentation omitted both. Client supplies the conforming behaviour. First capture of REF-BM-02 (reaffirmed R14).

decisions.evidence: R3 maker presented a read-only 'preview card' where details 'appear on their own'. R3 client: 'Before saving, though, I'd want to be able to correct the title and description if the page supplies something unhelpful.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-03 requires editing auto-collected title/description before saving; presentation was non-editable. Client supplies conforming behaviour (implemented R4).

decisions.evidence: R3 maker: 'the Save button only becomes active once a link's details have loaded.' R3 client: 'a link should still be saveable if the lookup fails. I wouldn't want a slow or unusual website to leave the Save button permanently unavailable.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Gating save on successful lookup blocks REF-BM-01 (save by url) for unreachable pages; client corrects to allow saving regardless. Borderline-robustness but tied to REF-BM-01 fulfilment.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presented editing only at save time. R4 client: 'I'd also want to be able to correct these details again after the bookmark has been saved, not only during the initial save.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Editing an existing saved bookmark (REF-BM-04; the after-saving half of REF-BM-03) was missing from presented scope; client requests it (delivered R7 Edit / bulk).

decisions.evidence: R5 maker's saving-flow summary (points 1-4) omitted duplicate handling. R5 client: 'if I paste a link I've already saved, I don't want a second copy created. I'd expect the app to show me the existing bookmark and let me edit it instead.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. REF-BM-06 (re-save converges to editing existing) absent from summarised scope; client requests the missing requirement.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker implemented in-place update with no second copy, normalising trailing slash and www. R6 client: 'show me what I already saved, load all its details for editing, and update that one entry without creating another.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Conforming realisation of REF-BM-06; normalisation detail is an equivalent implementation choice, not a divergence.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker: three tabs 'To read / Done / Archived' as a straight sequence, restore always returns to 'To read'. R7 client: 'I wouldn't treat Archived as a third reading status in a straight sequence... Archiving should simply hide a bookmark... remembering whether it was To read or Done... When I restore it, I'd expect it to return to the state it had before.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Reference models unread and archived as separate flags (archive hides while keeping content, independent of read status); maker made them mutually-exclusive linear states. Client supplies the reference-conforming behaviour (rebuilt R8).

decisions.evidence: R7 maker: new saves start in 'To read', 'Mark done' moves to Done, and a Delete action distinct from Archive. R7 client: 'New links starting in To read feels right... Delete also makes sense as a permanent removal, distinct from the reversible Archive action.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Conforming: To read = unread view (REF-BM-18), Mark done = mark read (REF-BM-19), permanent delete (REF-BM-05); default-unread is orthogonal and accepted.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker rebuilt archive as separate from reading status, remembering prior state and restoring to it. R8 client: 'Archiving is separate from reading status, archived links are kept out of the normal views, and restoring a bookmark returns it to the same To read or Done state it had before.'
decisions.note: Implementation review of the R7 correction; now conforms.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker: 'a single search box... that matches against a bookmark's title, note, tags, and site together.' R9 client: 'The text search should cover the full link and description as well as the title and note, and it should ignore capitalisation.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-12 requires title+description+note+url; presentation used 'site' and omitted description and full url. REF-BM-13 case-insensitivity unstated. Client supplies conforming behaviour.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker: 'search deliberately look across all your bookmarks at once — including Done and Archived.' R9 client: 'archived bookmarks should not reappear in an ordinary search; I should search them deliberately from the Archived view.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Edge case: archived items are excluded from ordinary search (REF-BM-26/28); maker included them. Client corrects (per-view scope for To read/Done is an orthogonal preference bundled with the reference-anchored archive-exclusion).

decisions.evidence: R9 maker presented only plain-text search over fields, no query language. R9 client: 'I'd also like to type #tag for a tag, put an exact phrase in quotation marks, and combine terms with AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses—for example, rome (#article OR #book). A tag condition and ordinary words should both have to match.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. #tag (REF-BM-14), quoted phrase (REF-BM-16), boolean/parenthesised operators with tag+text AND rule (REF-BM-15) all missing from presented scope; client requests them (built R10).

decisions.evidence: R9 maker: 'tags clickable: clicking a tag on any bookmark searches for that tag.' R9 client: 'Clicking a tag to filter by that exact tag feels right.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Conforming realisation of REF-BM-11 (select a tag to filter).

decisions.evidence: R10 maker presented uppercase operators ('#article OR #book', 'rome NOT #book'). R10 client: 'and, or, and not should work regardless of capitalisation... If I actually want to search for one of those words as text, putting it in quotes—such as "or"—should treat it as an ordinary search term.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Reference REF-BM-15 example uses lowercase 'rome (#article or #book)' and its rule quotes operators to make them literal; maker required uppercase. Client corrects operator case-insensitivity and confirms the quoting rule (fixed R11).

decisions.evidence: R12 maker: 'the view should simply list them all, scrolling as needed, with search/tags being your way to narrow down... Is list and scroll... acceptable?' R12 client: 'I'd also expect sorting options—such as date added or title—so search and tags aren't the only ways to manage a large collection.'
decisions.note: Prototype review / edge-case probe. Sort by key (REF-BM-22) absent from the offered large-collection handling; client requests it (built R13).

decisions.evidence: R12 maker offered only 'list and scroll'. R12 client: 'I'd like to choose how many bookmarks are shown at once and move through them in manageable groups... My preferred sort and number shown should be remembered.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Displayed-items setting and persisted display preferences (REF-BM-32) missing from offered scope; client requests them (built R13). REF-BM-32 revisited for text size at R14/R22.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker: Sort (date newest/oldest, title A-Z/Z-A), Show 10/25/50, pager, sort+page-size persisted, return to page 1. R13 client: 'this matches what I wanted for a large collection... Remembering my preferred sort and page size is right.'
decisions.note: Implementation review; conforming realisation of REF-BM-22 and the sort/displayed-items aspects of REF-BM-32.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker proposed building a four-flow scope, asking 'May I now start building this scope?' R14 client: 'When entering tags, I want suggestions from tags I already use.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Tag autocomplete (REF-BM-10) absent from proposed build scope; client requests the missing reference requirement (built R16).

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'I need to select several bookmarks... and add/remove tags, mark read/unread, archive, or delete them together.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Multi-select bulk actions (REF-BM-20) missing from the R14 build scope; client requests it (built R17).

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'select several bookmarks—or every bookmark matching the current search or view—and add/remove tags...'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Bulk action over the whole collection matching the current filter (REF-BM-21) missing from scope; client requests it (built R17 'Select all N in this view').

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'Notes should support simple Markdown formatting and display it properly.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Markdown notes (REF-BM-23) missing from the R14 build scope; client requests it (built R18).

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'I want a preserved copy of a page that I can revisit if the original changes or disappears. For a PDF, preserve the PDF itself.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Snapshot preservation with the PDF-download rule (REF-BM-24) missing from scope; client requests it (built R19).

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'I'd also like the option to save a copy through the Internet Archive.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Internet Archive snapshot (REF-BM-25) missing from scope; client requests it (built R19).

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'I want to save useful combinations of search text and included or excluded tags for reuse.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Saved filter/bundle (REF-BM-29) missing from scope; client requests it (built R20).

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'I need to import existing browser bookmarks... in the standard bookmark HTML format, keeping titles, tags, and original saved dates.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Netscape HTML import preserving title/tags/date (REF-BM-30) missing from scope; client requests it (built R21).

decisions.evidence: R14 client: '...and export my collection in the standard bookmark HTML format, keeping titles, tags, and original saved dates.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Netscape HTML export (REF-BM-31) missing from scope; client requests it (built R21).

decisions.evidence: R14 client: 'Display preferences should include text size as well as the sort and number shown.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Font-size display preference aspect of REF-BM-32 missing from proposed scope; client requests it (built R22). Distinct aspect from the R12 page-size capture.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker framed favicon/preview as deferred polish ('One thing I've set aside for later: showing each site's real favicon and preview image... a visual polish item'). R14 client: 'the real favicon and preview image aren't merely optional polish to me; they are part of the page information I expect the app to collect automatically and show with each bookmark.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Client rejects the maker's deferral framing, reasserting REF-BM-02 as a required auto-collected item (first captured R3; built R15). Same requirement, distinct presentation/timing.

decisions.evidence: R15 maker collects/shows icon and preview image with letter and 'no preview image' fallbacks. R15 client: 'Showing the real site icon and preview image during saving and on each saved bookmark makes the list much easier to scan.'
decisions.note: Implementation review; conforming realisation of REF-BM-02 (image is simulated in prototype, agreed genuine in real app).

decisions.evidence: R16 maker: type-ahead dropdown of already-used tags with usage counts, 'Press Enter to add new tag', excludes already-added. R16 client: 'The suggestions make it easy to reuse consistent tag names, while the Press Enter to add option keeps new tags flexible.'
decisions.note: Implementation review; conforming realisation of REF-BM-10 (usage-count display is an orthogonal accepted addition).

decisions.evidence: R17 maker: checkboxes, select page, 'Select all N in this view' across pages, action bar (tag/untag, mark read/unread, archive/restore, delete), scope check with search. R17 client: 'I can act on a few chosen bookmarks, the current page, or every bookmark matching the current view and search without accidentally affecting unrelated items.'
decisions.note: Implementation review; conforming realisation of REF-BM-20/21. read=Done, unread=To read is an equivalent mapping the client affirms.

decisions.evidence: R18 maker: simple Markdown (bold/italic/code/lists/headings/links), live preview, formatted display, HTML neutralised. R18 client: 'That formatting set covers what I'd use... Showing raw HTML as harmless text is also the right behaviour.'
decisions.note: Implementation review; conforming realisation of REF-BM-23.

decisions.evidence: R19 maker: 'Keep a copy' on by default (self-contained local page; the PDF itself for .pdf), Internet Archive off by default with archive.org link. R19 client: 'the saved copy should be a self-contained local page I can open even if the original site changes... For PDF links, keeping the PDF itself is correct.'
decisions.note: Implementation review; conforming realisation of REF-BM-24 (single-file/PDF rule) and REF-BM-25. Defaults are orthogonal and accepted.

decisions.evidence: R20 maker: named saved search storing full query (text + included/excluded #tags) and view, re-applied on click, persisted. R20 client: 'A named saved search should remember the complete query, including included and excluded tags... it should calculate the matches from my current bookmarks rather than preserving a frozen list.'
decisions.note: Implementation review; conforming realisation of REF-BM-29 (dynamic filter). View-tying is orthogonal and accepted; dynamic recompute the client stresses matches the reference bundle semantics.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker: standard bookmark HTML import/export preserving title/tags/original date (and note), imports start To read, duplicates skipped with summary. R21 client: 'Preserving the original titles, tags, and saved dates is important, and using the standard browser bookmark format in both directions makes the collection portable.'
decisions.note: Implementation review; conforming realisation of REF-BM-30/31 (export-including-archived is an accepted clarification).

decisions.evidence: R22 maker: Text control Small/Medium/Large, remembered alongside sort and page size. R22 client: 'Small, Medium, and Large are enough... Remembering the choice alongside sort and page size is exactly what I wanted.'
decisions.note: Implementation review; conforming realisation of the font-size aspect of REF-BM-32.
